subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap & pilot next steps

Hi Leah —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we’re aligned on fit for Redwood Dedicated. I kept this tight; happy to expand any section.

Summary of pain points you described:
- Unpredictable latency during daily spikes (impacting auth & checkout flows)
- Noisy-neighbor interference on shared endpoints; need stronger isolation for compliance
- Lack of predictable throughput for model bundles used in risk scoring and chat ops

What you told us about current stack & constraints:
- Infra: AWS EKS + internal API gateway, logs to Splunk; models currently self-hosted (Llama-2 family, quantized variants)
- Typical sustained inference load: ~200–300 TPS; peak spikes to ~450 TPS during batch rollouts
- Success criteria: p99 latency target <= 200–250ms for 8k-context models, consistent throughput during peak windows, SOC2 evidence & audit trail for production traffic

Why Dedicated looks like a fit (summary):
- Reserved GPU pools give predictable per-token latency and throughput without cross-tenant interference
- Isolation (VPC peering + customer-only nodes) addresses compliance and audit requirements
- Autoscaling + controlled burst path preserves baseline SLAs while allowing temporary surge capacity

Sizing / autoscale / burst assumptions we discussed:
- Baseline recommendation: reserved pool sized to cover your typical sustained TPS (200–300 TPS); we suggested starting 3–4 H100-equivalent GPUs for your initial baseline depending on model variant and quantization.
- Burst policy: allow bursts to a shared overflow pool for up to ~500 TPS for 15 minutes with a cooldown; fallback routing to a compatible smaller model variant if overflow is unavailable.
- Autoscale triggers: queue depth > 100 requests for 60s, sustained GPU util > 70% for 2 minutes, health-checks to prevent noisy scale-ups.

Pilot proposal (next step):
- Two-week pilot: provision 1 reserved node in your target region with traffic replay of a representative window (we can replay from logs)
- Success metrics for pilot: p99 latency <= 250ms on baseline, zero cross-tenant faults, verified logging/audit events sent to your Splunk instance

Action items I’ll own:
- Share sizing worksheet and a draft pilot SOW (attached)
- Put together a short pricing band for both reserved commit and burst-overflow usage
- Schedule a technical kickoff with Vivek and Grace and your infra lead (suggest Wed 2026-12-08 10:00 PT)

Action items for FinPay:
- Confirm a representative traffic window for replay (1–2 hours) and a list of 2–3 model variants you plan to run in pilot
- Confirm procurement timeline and PO contact (we can loop Miguel if helpful)

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-proposal.pdf, Redwood-Dedicated-Sizing-Worksheet.xlsx

If this matches your read, I’ll book the kickoff and circulate the SOW for review.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Diego —

Appreciate the clear write-up. A couple clarifications from my side:
- Confirmation on stack: yes, EKS fronting via our internal gateway; logs to Splunk and metrics in Datadog.
- Models: mostly Llama-2 70B (quantized to 4-bit for production), occasional Llama-2-13B for lower-latency paths.
- Traffic profile: sustained ~250 TPS; spikes up to 450 TPS for ~10–20 minutes during morning batch runs.
- Compliance: SOC2 is required; we also need to see network topology diagrams for VPC peering and KMS integration details.

Open questions:
1) Cold-start times — for model shards that aren’t warm in KV cache, what should we expect?
2) Ballpark cost estimate for a 3–4 node reserved pool vs a 1-node pilot (we’re just evaluating CAPEX/OpEx tradeoffs internally).
3) Pilot length — we prefer 2 weeks but would like an option to extend by 1 week if we need extra replay runs.

I can confirm procurement timelines after I loop Miguel (procurement). We’re US-only for now, so region = us.

Thanks,
Leah Barnes
Head of AI Platform | FinPay Inc.
leah@finpay.co

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap & pilot next steps

Leah — great questions. Short answers below and notes on next steps.

1) Cold-start / KV cache behavior
- If a model’s KV cache is cold we typically see additional latency on the first few tokens while weights are loaded and caches populated. For quantized Llama-2 70B this is roughly 60–120ms additional on that initial request depending on sequence length.
- Pre-warming: we can keep a warm hot-path by keeping an idle warm slot (pre-warmed instance) which reduces cold-starts to <15–30ms for subsequent requests. For pilot we recommend enabling a single pre-warm slot.

2) Ballpark pricing (very rough, final will be in proposal):
- 1-node pilot (reserved for 2 weeks): nominal pilot fee + covered burst + SRE support for onboarding (we’ll include specifics in the SOW)
- 3–4 node reserved pool (monthly commit): pricing depends on node class; rough range: $20k–$60k/month depending on H100 vs A100-equivalent and network egress assumptions. We’ll send an explicit band after sizing worksheet input.

3) Pilot length & extension
- Two-week pilot with an optional 1-week extension is fine. We’ll include the extension clause in the SOW.

Attachments: SOW-template.docx (draft pilot scope), I also added the sizing worksheet again to the Drive link.

Next steps I’ll take this morning:
- Draft a short SOW for a 2-week pilot and share it for quick review
- Add estimated pricing bands after you complete the sizing worksheet
- Tentatively schedule kickoff Wed 2026-12-08 10:00 PT; if that works I’ll send a calendar invite and include Vivek and Grace for the technical portion

Finally — links: HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/7264/record/FP-7264; Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-finpay-pilot

Diego
